W03-MO01-S005-concurrency-1.claim: The message-ID guard can acknowledge an EventSub delivery before durable acceptance, losing the event if the original attempt fails or crashes.
W03-MO01-S005-concurrency-1.failure_scenario: Attempt A commits the guard for message M, then stalls before enqueueing stream.online or committing channel.subscription.end. An overlapping delivery B of M encounters that guard and receives a duplicate success, which the webhook returns as HTTP 204. A subsequently fails its database operation or the process terminates before persistence. No durable event exists despite B's acknowledgement. The crash variant also affects a later retry after restart while the 600-second guard remains active.
W03-MO01-S005-concurrency-1.evidence: At fixed SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, dispatch.rs:715-736 claims the guard and returns Ok for a losing claim before route runs at line 746. guard.rs:122-139 commits that claim independently through the pool and stores no completion state. Core enqueue happens later at dispatch.rs:810-813; subscription writes commit separately at telemetry.rs:131-164. webhook_receiver.rs:306-319 maps every Ok, including this premature duplicate, to 204. main.rs:1476-1483 serves the shared dispatcher without serializing requests. Static interleaving analysis only; no tests or probes executed.
W03-MO01-S005-concurrency-1.expected_behavior: Acknowledgement must mean the delivery has been durably accepted or successfully applied. dispatch.rs:682-683 explicitly treats failed acceptance as retryable, and the assigned regression at eventsub_dispatch.rs:1442-1451 requires rollback followed by processing the same message again, rather than suppressing it as a duplicate.
W03-MO01-S005-concurrency-1.countermeasures: The atomic guard prevents simultaneous claims but does not distinguish pending from completed acceptance. Releasing the guard on Err at dispatch.rs:761-775 helps sequential retries only: it cannot retract B's earlier 204 and never executes after a crash. Inbox retry and subscription transaction rollback protect existing work, not an event that was never durably accepted. The same premature-success branch covers both core enqueue and transactional subscription lifecycle routes.

W03-MO01-S005-concurrency-2.claim: Overlapping hype-train Begin and End writes can create an unfinished Begin plus a separate End and inflate the post-stream train count.
W03-MO01-S005-concurrency-2.failure_scenario: Valid Begin and End notifications for the same broadcaster and started_at overlap, for example after delayed delivery of Begin. End's UPDATE observes no committed Begin row. Begin then inserts its row, and End performs its fallback INSERT. Both calls succeed, leaving two rows for one train, with the Begin row's ended_at still NULL. The post-stream payload counts both rows and reports two trains instead of the single train reported by the ordered case.
W03-MO01-S005-concurrency-2.evidence: telemetry.rs:432-479 performs End's UPDATE and fallback INSERT as independent pool operations; Begin always inserts. dispatch.rs:937-950 handles these notifications inline, with distinct message-ID guards rather than per-train ordering. The table definition and hypertable migration provide no uniqueness constraint on broadcaster plus started_at. post_stream.rs:1195-1203 computes hype_trains.count using COUNT(*) without excluding the unfinished duplicate. The assigned ordered regression at eventsub_dispatch.rs:1314-1348 expects one row and a populated ended_at.
W03-MO01-S005-concurrency-2.expected_behavior: The documented normal case closes the existing Begin rather than creating an additional End row. However, behavior for reordered notifications is not explicitly specified, and Progress deliberately inserts snapshots. Consequently, changing reconciliation or snapshot semantics is not sufficiently established for automatic class-B fixing.
W03-MO01-S005-concurrency-2.countermeasures: Message dedup only protects repeated delivery IDs; Begin and End have different IDs. Neither the dispatcher nor the update/fallback sequence serializes the same train. The sequential regression cannot exercise this interleaving. Overview and monetization filter ended_at IS NOT NULL, limiting their immediate count impact, but the post-stream count includes the unfinished row. Class C because the intended out-of-order and snapshot contract needs clarification.

W03-MO01-S005-correctness-1.claim: stream.offline retries are silently discarded by their own 120-second throttle.
W03-MO01-S005-correctness-1.failure_scenario: An accepted stream.offline event for broadcaster 42 claims OfflineThrottle successfully, then apply_stream_offline fails transiently, for example because its UPDATE times out. The handler returns an error and the inbox schedules a retry. With the database healthy again within five seconds and no intervening stream.online, that retry finds the original 120-second throttle still active, returns Ok immediately, and is deleted from the inbox. The offline state UPDATE and the subsequent reannounce cooldown, score refresh, and offline hook never complete for this delivery.
W03-MO01-S005-correctness-1.evidence: Static proof at review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af, with no source drift in the inspected files. The primary test eventsub_dispatch.rs:720-810 establishes the offline effects; following its build_stack led to this production handler. handlers.rs:475-490 persists OfflineThrottle before any state finalization and treats an unsuccessful claim as success. The state write at :510-516 propagates errors without releasing OfflineThrottle. inbox_runtime.rs:268-288 schedules the first retry after one second; its default idle wait is five seconds (:20). On the retry's Ok return, :215-221 calls mark_delivered, which deletes the work in inbox_store/mod.rs:153-164. Production main.rs:1434-1455 wires this same handler and runtime.
W03-MO01-S005-correctness-1.expected_behavior: A failed durable inbox delivery must retry its unfinished effects rather than be acknowledged as successfully processed. inbox_runtime.rs:53-64 explicitly defines handler errors as retryable and guarantees at-least-once processing; handlers.rs:43-45 specifies releasing effect guards on failure. The primary offline test at eventsub_dispatch.rs:765-810 requires offline state, session finalization, and the offline hooks while suppressing genuinely duplicate completed effects.
W03-MO01-S005-correctness-1.countermeasures: run_business_effect_once releases only its BusinessEffect guard on error (handlers.rs:74-82), not the enclosing OfflineThrottle. MessageId dedup is applied when dispatching into the inbox, not when processing retries. Go-live releases OfflineThrottle (:256-259), but there is no go-live in this scenario. The poller may eventually repair live state, but its offline raid path also checks the same throttle (poller/engine.rs:166-195), and it does not restore the discarded inbox delivery. Targeted twin inspection covered the online release and poller claim paths; no additional confirmed twin is claimed. No tests or runtime probes were executed.

W03-MO01-S004-concurrency-1.claim: Expired inbox workers can resurrect delivered work as a dead-letter or overwrite newer retry state.

Processing exceeds its 30-second lease, so worker B leases the same row, completes it successfully and calls mark_delivered. A subsequently fails its stale attempt and calls mark_dead_letter. That method inserts the cached LeasedWork unconditionally, although the inbox row no longer exists, creating a dead-letter for successfully delivered work. The same missing ownership check affects mark_retry: a delayed attempt with an older attempt_count can overwrite a newer consumer's higher counter and lease deadline, reducing recorded attempts and making actively leased work available again.

Lines 218-249 insert/upsert dead-letter data from the cached work before deleting the inbox row, without checking whether that row exists or still belongs to this attempt. An expired attempt must not overwrite a newer attempt's lease or reduce its retry counter. The shared-consumer contract is explicit in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/crates/tb-monitoring/src/inbox_store/mod.rs:4-9. The dead-letter transaction prevents a partial move but does not validate ownership or the continued existence of the source row. Separate work_id primary keys in /home/nathanael/.worktrees/tb-vollreview-artefakte/rust/migrations/20260601000000_baseline_schema.sql:2087,2094 do not prevent this race.
